video_title: How Harden HELPED The Cavs Get Better - Is It Enough??

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's contract situation with the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: James Harden opted out of a contract that would have paid him 43 million this year.
quotes.quote: To allow this to happen, remember that James Harden opted out of a contract that would have paid him 43 million this year. That contract was not fully guaranteed. It was only guaranteed 12 million. But the truth is the Cavs were not going to cut him. He is their starting, he is their franchise point guard. So if he opted into that contract, they would have paid him the 43 million. He was getting the money. James Harden was willing to opt out of that contract and sit around all summer and basically pick up the phone whenever the Cavs called, calling his agents more than anything, and say, 'Yeah, I'll go down a little farther, I'll go down a little farther.' And so, as the Cavs made various moves, Harden not only was willing to reduce his salary, but he was willing to recruit.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's new three-year contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: James Harden gets a three-year, 97 million dollar contract, all guaranteed.
quotes.quote: James Harden gets a three-year, 97 million dollar contract, all guaranteed, and the third year is a player option.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Cleveland Cavaliers' roster depth and salary cap challenges
quotes.excerpt: the Cavs are all in on right now and they're trying to kind of, which is a tough spot
quotes.quote: The Cavs are all in on right now and they're trying to kind of, which is a tough spot to be, you're all in on right now with real questions about your bench and not a whole lot of ways you can go about upgrading. I don't think they're hard cap now as well. So to upgrade the bench even during the season is going to be extremely difficult to be able to pull that off.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's role as a secondary ball-handler for the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: He reminds me of a young Paul George.
quotes.quote: He will be their secondary ball-handler in the lineup when one of their guards is sitting, I would think a lot of times. But I remember I was talking to Aaron Gordon, he said, 'Dude, we see this stuff when we play pickup and things like that, we've seen it for a while.' He said, 'He reminds me of a young Paul George.' Now, I think there might be hyperbole there, you know, young Paul George is awfully good, but his point was he looked at Watson as a really dynamic, athletic, versatile 6-8 wing.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The tradeability of James Harden's new contract
quotes.excerpt: When a contract gets signed, I ask the question, can this contract be traded?
quotes.quote: When a contract gets signed, I ask the question, can this contract be traded? I've talked to executives today who have said, 'I don't like that contract.' But I've also talked to executives who have said, 'He's 23 years old, that's probably going to age pretty well.' If he was 33 years old, I wouldn't like it, but 23 years old, I like it. So I don't think they could trade it for huge value this afternoon.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden joining the 500 million dollar career earnings club
quotes.excerpt: James Harden is now going to become the fourth player in league history to make over half a billion dollars.
quotes.quote: Shams had reporting in his story that he is now going to become the fourth player in league history to make over half a billion dollars in salary. And obviously the other three are the Olympic teammates in 24 and LeBron James, Kevin Durant and Stephen Curry.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' decision to trade James Harden last season
quotes.excerpt: There was some point in December or January where the Clippers decided they were pulling the plug.
quotes.quote: There was some point in December or January where the Clippers decided they were pulling the plug. They got off to that bad start and then they got hot, but they didn't believe in the team. Obviously they traded Ivica Zubac, they obviously traded Harden and then eventually they traded Kawhi, if that ever actually goes through.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The role of agents in the James Harden trade to Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: That trade to Cleveland was manufactured by the agents. The agents went out and found the deal.
quotes.quote: That trade to Cleveland was manufactured by the agents. The agents went out and found the deal. Now the Cavs liked him and were watching the situation too. So they go out, just like the deal to Washington was partially executed by CAA. The part of the reason that Trey Mann is now in Washington is because Will Dawkins, the GM, drafted him when he was in Oklahoma City. There's all these things that happen, but they get Harden into a spot where they're willing to pay him.
